meta.probingQuestion: What does your friction do to the people across from you?
meta.connection: You can pin someone hard and still keep them safe. That is control of your own force. Your conflict off the mat lands on real people too, and the same control applies: honest friction, not harm.
meta.takeaway: Friction is fine. Harm is a choice. The control is yours.

slides.title: What does your friction do to the people across from you?

items: The overhook player wins when the underhook player falls to his hips or hands.
The underhook player wins by closing his hands under the elbows.
The bottom player wins by standing up and reaching the hips, or by making the top player's back touch the mat.
The top player wins with shin contact on the knees or body.
The top player holds as long as he keeps the grip.
The bottom player wins by breaking the grip.
